`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes: all 7 tests run with no failures. I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and corrected one test that was itself wrong.

**Code fixes (`household/bills.py`)**
1. **`split_bill` dropped the leftover cents.** It returned `[total // people] * people`, so 1001 split 2 ways came out as `[500, 500]` and lost a cent. It now splits off the leftover with `divmod` and gives one extra cent to each of the first people, as the docstring says. 1001 split 2 ways is now `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates` crashed when the payments crossed into a new year.** It added `i` to the month without wrapping, so it asked for month 13 and raised `IllegalMonthError`. It now carries the extra months into the year, so starting from Nov 30 you get Dec 30 and then Jan 30 of the next year.

**Test change (`tests/test_bills.py`) — please check this one**
`test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`. That adds up to 999, which breaks the function's own promise that the shares add up to exactly the total. Once the remainder is handed out properly, that test fails. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you actually meant shares to round down and drop the leftover, then the docstring and `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first` are the parts that need to change instead.

I haven't committed anything.
